rows.subtype: Restless and asking what to do [Actor]
rows.description: A child declares boredom after ten minutes and wants a screen; boredom is uncomfortable but can also be the doorway to imagination when adults give time and simple materials.

A pupil hears a flat, monotone voice from a tired teacher or a shy friend. It can show boredom, low mood, calm or a personal speaking style, including some neurodivergent voices, so it should not be read as not caring.

Sustaining effort on multi-month goals despite boredom and setbacks.

rows.subtype: Hiding behind a parent at a party [Actor]
rows.description: A child clings to a parent's leg and refuses to greet anyone; staying away from the scary thing feels like relief, and gentle nearness helps more than pushing.
We talked daily and then they vanished. It feels like erasure. Wise: recognise it reflects their avoidance, not my worth; grieve, and ask friends for company. Harmful: fake accounts to check on them.
A child who fears being wrong will only do puzzles they already know how to solve; avoiding failure feels safe but also blocks learning.

A teenager under exam or assignment pressure copies work and tells themselves it is just this once. Fear of failure and a common culture of copying make it feel normal, while the habit erodes their own ability.
A child who takes longer with reading calls themselves dumb and stops trying; a single label replaces a specific skill that can be practised.

A teenager may cry while explaining something angry, or laugh until they cry. Mixed tears can mean overwhelmed feeling, joy, relief or tension, so labelling them from the outside can be wrong; asking helps.
A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.

rows.subtype: Playlists and dance trends as mood signals [Mismatch]
rows.description: A teenager shares a sad song or a viral dance video online, which may mean mood, humour, belonging or mere fashion. A brief kind check-in works better than assuming distress from one post.
